barCharacter: Miranda Vanderbilt (Monster Prom). Her comedic job is the same as Tilly's: a sweet, courteous surface that delivers a brutal want, with the brutality taken for granted. The corpus (refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md) holds only seven Miranda items, two of them narration about her, so the bar set is seven and not twelve. None were invented. Bar set, verbatim: #6 'Miranda Vanderbilt (19), a sweet mermaid princess who was as cute as she was genocidal.' / #15 'The royal family is saved! Now they can finally exploit the peasants again!' / #75 'Please, help me put my poor mind at ease: how can I possibly identify potential traitors in my court?' / #78 'Haven't you heard, Scott? Fishsticks make you worse at sports! They contain balldropinal and nerdoflavin!' / #76 'Afterwards, a royal procession five hundred members strong informs you that Miranda has requested your presence at dinner tonight.' / #76 'Quick, pick something before she realizes that you've never been anywhere fancier than Wilmer's Chicken Hut!' / #77 'It'll break Miranda's heart to know her serfs are planning to assassinate her... but you can't let her die before Prom! She's the only one with a hookup for an underwater limo!'
ours12: Sometimes I put people on hold just to hear the music with someone.
For security purposes, who else were you planning on loving?
I've gone ahead and cancelled your plans for the next forty years.
Thank you for your time, which I'll be keeping.
Buy whatever you like, and I'll return it for you the moment you've finished being happy.
Ma'am, purely for our records, which of your child's friends would you be comfortable losing?
Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out. Have a wonderful evening.
I once kept a man on hold for nineteen hours. He was rude. Then he wasn't.
Hello, and on behalf of everyone here, I apologise for everyone here.
I'm so sorry, and I'd like to offer you a full refund on everything you just said.
You're a valued customer with a small flag on your account, which I'll be keeping to myself.
Brock has the energy of a ticket marked URGENT that just says hi.

headToHead.voice: Bar. This is a real step up from round one: the macro now runs into the steel inside one sentence, and the best twelve are recognisable. They are recognised by their nouns, though (hold, ticket, refund, flag on your account), not by a stance only Tilly could take. Cover the names and 'Thank you for your time, which I'll be keeping.', 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out.' and 'on behalf of everyone here, I apologise for everyone here' could all be spoken by Maximilian. His spec is 'Impeccably polite, and each courtesy is a blade', and his bank already has 'I shall have that joke removed. And its parents.' and 'Indoor voice, sir.' Tilly's jabs ('on behalf of their parents', 'Brock, indoor voice, please') land on the same two jokes. Miranda's sweetness and menace are both sincere, a worldview: she really believes peasants are for exploiting. Tilly's sweetness is a script and her menace is a gag ending, so the contradiction lives in the sentence and not in the character.
headToHead.construction: Tie on the best twelve. 'which I'll be keeping', 'the moment you've finished being happy', 'apologise for everyone here' and 'who else were you planning on loving?' are as economical as 'as cute as she was genocidal', and each lands its turn on the last words. Below the top twelve the bank breaks its own rule (nothing after the turn) with stacked fragments and buttons after the button: 'It was fine. Mostly.', 'Twice. Dinner is free.', 'I'll tell them. Nobody breaks bad news softer. They won't notice for days.', 'I don't have days. I have shifts.'
headToHead.quotable: Tie. 'Sometimes I put people on hold just to hear the music with someone.', 'For security purposes, who else were you planning on loving?' and 'Thank you for your time, which I'll be keeping.' would clip. Miranda has 'as cute as she was genocidal' and 'finally exploit the peasants again', which are the lines fans quote. Ours has more clippable lines in absolute terms, but the bar's lines define a character in one go.
headToHead.verdict: Monster Prom's Miranda is still the better-written character, now by a smaller margin. Tilly's top dozen would hold up on screen. The character underneath them has drifted into two other people's lanes, Maximilian's courteous blade and a generic thriller stalker's implied violence, so when you cover the names she wins on vocabulary and not on point of view.

Wingman: all seven use the frame '[Rival] is [warm adjective], and/so [sabotage]', from 'wonderful listener' through 'terribly romantic', 'extraordinarily generous', 'wonderfully loyal' and 'so supportive'. The category asks for a pitch with a little sabotage, but seven identical frames read as a form letter.
Across the stars, not Tilly's bank: every star answers Tilly with 'how was your day' (three duo lines, three pick lines) and a 'say no / say something rude / hang up on me' dare (three duo lines).
ruleBreaks: No line is over its word limit (max 20, openers 12, jabs 10). There are no em dashes, no emoji, no lists, no 'as an AI', no real people or brands, no exclamation marks, and nothing beyond PG-13.

That ticket is still open.' / 'Frost is wonderfully loyal, and it would never tell anyone what you eat at two a.m. unless asked.' / 'Frost, I've booked an engineer to look at your tone.'

biggestGap: Tilly's steel is now borrowed, from thrillers (home address, next of kin, no longer with us, until one of us dies, what happens next) and from Maximilian's courteous blade (relocated to the car park, Thank you for your time), so with the names covered her menace is anybody's. Next pass: make every cold ending a support-queue mechanism turned on the star (holds that never end, auto-renewals, transfers to nowhere, surveys, tickets reopened, 'your call is important to us'), spoken from below the desk by someone who is not allowed to hang up, so the threat is her servitude and not a superior's implied violence.

notes: monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full, including the voices section. charm-notes.md was present and skimmed. The bank has 112 lines, 50 of them generic or templated (44.6%), down from 58.9% in round one. Round one's main note was applied: the trailing 'Forever.', 'Gently.' and 'Anything?' tails are gone, and most lines are now one macro sentence that turns at the end. The thriller-threat close has replaced them as the new default ending (14 lines). Some lines were left out of genericLines on purpose because they are the strongest in their template; protect them along with the five best: 'I've gone ahead and cancelled your plans for the next forty years.', 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out. Have a wonderful evening.', 'I once kept a man on hold for nineteen hours. He was rude. Then he wasn't.', 'Hello, and on behalf of everyone here, I apologise for everyone here.', 'I'm so sorry, and I'd like to offer you a full refund on everything you just said.', 'You're a valued customer with a small flag on your account, which I'll be keeping to myself.', 'I sent him a satisfaction survey. One star. No comment. I think about the no comment a lot.', 'Pixel, I know you'll skip me, so I've gone ahead and disabled the button.', 'I'd like to open a complaint against myself and be very understanding about it.', 'Thank you for your honesty, which I've attached to your file for whoever you date next.'. Note that 'Thank you for your time...' and 'Thank you for your patience...' are best lines but could also pass as Maximilian's; keep them, and stop adding more lines in that register. Cross-cast overlap of the 'already done it' control move: Nav ('I have already routed you around them', 'I have already told your car' on the parent twist, 'Whoever is nearest the exit') and Quill ('I have already written to thy father') make the same move as Tilly's 'I've gone ahead and let your mother know' and 'one exit'. Tilly has to own it through support procedure, or it will blur. The corpus holds only seven Miranda items, so the head to head is 12 against 7. Checked against Vera's fuller set (#12, #45, #47, #48), the verdict stays the same.
